Data sources and interpretation

Source: vignettes/data-sources.Rmd
data-sources.Rmd

contentiousR standardizes country and year keys; it does not make the underlying research designs interchangeable. Cite each source used in an analysis and consult its codebook for definitions, scope, and limitations.

How each bundled file was prepared from its official release (compression, format conversion, dropped columns) is documented in data-raw/PREPROCESSING.md.

Argument Bundled version and coverage Unit returned Source
GDP: "gapminder" Gapminder v32 Country-year Gapminder
GDP: "fariss" Fariss et al. 2022, latent estimate, 1500–2019 Country-year Dataverse
Population: "wpp" UN World Population Prospects 2024, 1949–2023 Country-year UN Population Division
Population: "nmc" National Material Capabilities v7.0, 1816–2022 Country-year Correlates of War
Population: "fariss" Fariss et al. 2022, latent estimate, 1500–2019 Country-year Dataverse
Military expenditure: "sipri" SIPRI Military Expenditure Database v1.2, 1949–2025 Country-year SIPRI
Military expenditure: "nmc" National Material Capabilities v7.0, 1816–2022 Country-year Correlates of War
Military expenditure: "barnum" Barnum et al. 2025, latent estimate, 1816–2019 Country-year Dataverse
"navco1.3" NAVCO 1.3, 1900–20191 Campaign onset Dataverse
"navco2.1" NAVCO 2.1, 1945–2013 Campaign-year Dataverse

"csra" (CSRA Revolutionary Database v1.102) was removed in version 0.2.0: the database has been renamed RAQED, so use "raqed".

Package-related transformations and explanations

SCAD repeats events when they span multiple locations. For country-level use, contentiousR retains one row per positive event ID before aggregating. Its documented -99, -88, and -77 death-count values are represented as missing rather than as negative deaths.

UCDP/PRIO expands conflicts with multiple location codes before aggregation. ucdp_prio_incidence marks any active conflict in a country-year, while ucdp_prio_onset is one only when start_date2 falls in that year. The VPP file has no equivalent episode-start field; ucdp_vpp_onset is retained only as a backwards-compatible alias of ucdp_vpp_incidence.

Mass Mobilization reports participant size through a mixture of exact numbers, ranges, inequalities, and qualitative strings. mm_participants contains the maximum of exact numeric reports. mm_participants_reported preserves all reported strings so users can apply a substantively appropriate recoding.

Legacy campaign and episode sources can contain several rows for one country-year. add_conflict(aggregate = TRUE) reports their count and takes a missing-safe maximum of numeric fields. Use aggregate = FALSE or call conflict_data() directly when campaign-level observations are required.

Unmatched panel rows remain NA, because absence from a source is not always evidence of zero events.

MEC contains 2,734 reformist and maximalist contentious episodes worldwide. contentiousR preserves its episode-level rows and all published variables, using the source’s byear (beginning year) as year. Fourteen left-censored episodes have a mec_bdate before 1955 but a source byear of 1955. With add_conflict(aggregate = TRUE), MEC follows the same explicit aggregation policy as the other campaign and episode sources; use aggregate = FALSE to retain individual episodes.

RAQED (the Revolutionary and Quasi-revolutionary Episodes Dataset, the successor of the CSRA Revolutionary Database) is kept at its episode level, with the episode’s start_year as year. Its type column distinguishes revolutionary episodes (RE), questionable revolutionary episodes (RE?), and quasi-revolutionary episodes (QRE); raqed_type_re, raqed_type_re_q, and raqed_type_qre are the matching dummies, so that add_conflict() can aggregate them. Abkhazia, Hong Kong, Palestine, Puerto Rico, and Western Sahara have no COW or Gleditsch-Ward code and are dropped.

OMG is coded by campaign phase: a campaign that pauses and resumes has one row per phase. contentiousR keeps the phase rows with the phase’s start_year as year. omg_phase_onset is one for every phase, while omg_onset is one only for a campaign’s first phase, so a resumed campaign is not counted as a new onset. OMG identifies countries by V-Dem country_id; Serbia is mapped to COW 345 / GW 340, Yemen to COW 678 before 1990 and 679 afterwards (GW 678), and Piedmont-Sardinia to 325 (Italy). Hong Kong, Palestine, and Western Sahara are dropped. OMG has coded only a subset of countries so far, so a missing country-year means “not coded or no campaign”, not “no campaign”. The bundled file omits the source’s free-text notes, source lists, and coder names.

ARC 2.0 records the formal organizations that took part in 28,683 protest and armed-conflict events in Africa, Latin America, and the Caribbean. The events themselves come from SCAD and the UCDP Georeferenced Event Dataset (GED), so "arc" overlaps with "scad"; what it adds is organizational participation and the maximalist/non-maximalist coding of demands. Events are counted in the year they start. arc_n_events_org and arc_share_events_org count events with at least one identified organization, and arc_n_orgs counts distinct organizations active in a country-year. Every GED event is coded as maximalist in the source.

NAVCO 3.0 records individual actions in 26 countries, coded by actor: anti-government campaigns (actor_id 2), the state (1), and international, non-aligned, and local state actors. nvc3.0_onset is one when at least one campaign action occurred in the period and zero when the period has only actions by other actors, so it is not comparable with the campaign onsets of NAVCO 1.3 and 2.1. Tactics (nvc3.0_n_nonviolent, nvc3.0_n_violent, nvc3.0_n_mixed) and regime-change goals are counted for campaign actions only; state responses are counted from st_posture (concessions 1–3, repression 5–7, lethal repression 7). The source records fatalities, injuries, and participant numbers either as a number or as a range such as “100-300”; contentiousR keeps both bounds, as _low and _high columns.

Mass Mobilization includes rows with protest = 0 for country-years in which no protest was recorded. These give mm_onset = 0 and mm_n_protests = 0. Versions up to 0.1.0 counted them as protests.

Country-quarter, country-month, and country-day panels

build_states_panel(unit = "quarter"), unit = "month", and unit = "day" build panels at a finer unit. add_conflict() then places every event or episode in the quarter, month, or day of its start date. This needs a date at least as precise as the unit (a quarter needs the month), so:

Dataset Quarter, month Day Records dropped at a finer unit
"scad", "mmad", "arc", "navco3.0", "raqed", "mec" Yes Yes None
"mm" Yes Yes Country-years without protest (no date)
"beissinger" Yes Yes 5 dated by year only (quarter, month); 56 dated by month only (day)
"omg" Yes Yes Phases dated by year only (quarter, month) or by month only (day)
"navco1.3", "navco2.1", "ucdp_prio", "ucdp_vpp" No No —

add_conflict() reports how many records it drops. Annual data (GDP, population, military expenditure, V-Dem) are joined by year, so all periods of a year share that year’s value. add_leader_data() uses the leaders’ dates in office instead: each period gets the leader in power at its end, so Egypt has Mubarak in January 2011 and Tantawi from February. REIGN records the month, not the day, a leader left office, so it supports quarters and months but not days. add_lag() and add_spell_duration() count periods in the panel’s unit.

aggregate_panel() collapses a finer panel to a coarser unit: counts are summed, indicators and maxima take the maximum, and annual data and leaders take the value of the last period. Lags and spell counters are dropped, as they need to be recomputed at the new unit. A monthly panel aggregated to years gives the same event counts as a yearly panel.

list_datasets() lists every dataset with its years, countries, record type, the units it supports, and its column prefix.

Missing records: NA or 0?

A period without a record can mean that nothing happened, or that the source does not cover that country and year. By default add_conflict() leaves both as NA. With fill_zero = TRUE, it sets event indicators and counts to 0 where the dataset covers the country-year and keeps NA elsewhere. Coverage is defined per dataset (the zero_fill column of list_datasets()):

Datasets A country-year is covered if
"navco1.3", "navco2.1", "beissinger", "raqed", "mec", "omg", "ucdp_prio", "ucdp_vpp" it is in the dataset’s years (global coverage)
"scad", "arc", "navco3.0" the country has at least one record, and the year is in the dataset’s years
"mm" the source lists it, including country-years it codes as having no protest
"mmad" it lies between the country’s first and last year with a record

MMAD covers autocracies, but the package does not ship MMAD’s list of autocratic country-years, so the last rule is an approximation. A 0 inside a country’s span can still be a period MMAD did not code: MMAD has no events in Egypt from July to December 2012, and fill_zero = TRUE gives 0 there. Maxima, means, and descriptive columns are never filled.

Episodes in progress

Onset columns mark the period in which an episode started. For NAVCO 1.3, NAVCO 2.1, Beissinger, RAQED, MEC, and OMG, add_conflict() also adds <prefix>incidence (1 if an episode was in progress) and <prefix>n_active (how many), from each episode’s start to its end date. Where the end date is less precise than the panel’s unit, the episode runs to the end of the period the source gives: an OMG phase that ended “in 2005” is active through December 2005. Beissinger gives durations rather than end dates; an episode ends at its start date plus the duration in days (or in calendar months, if the start is known only to the month). Episodes the source codes as ongoing run to the end of its coverage.

UN WPP reports today’s countries, with population reconstructed back to 1949 within today’s borders, while the panels follow the states of each year. load_population_data(dataset = "wpp") therefore assigns every WPP country to the state that governed it in each year:

  • States that later split are the sum of their parts while they existed: the USSR (the fifteen republics until 1991), Yugoslavia and Serbia and Montenegro (Serbia, Kosovo, Montenegro, and the other republics until they became states), Czechoslovakia, Ethiopia with Eritrea (1952-1992), Pakistan with Bangladesh (to 1970), Sudan with South Sudan (to 2010), Indonesia with Timor-Leste (1976-2001), Malaysia with Singapore (1963-1964), and Egypt with Syria (1959-1960). Hong Kong is part of China from 1997 and Macao from 1999.
  • States formed by unification cannot be split back into their parts, so those parts are NA before unification: West and East Germany before 1990, North and South Yemen before 1990, North and South Vietnam before 1976, and Tanganyika and Zanzibar before 1964. For the same reason Abkhazia and South Ossetia (included in Georgia) and Tibet in 1949-1950 (included in China) have no WPP data.
  • Territories that were not part of any state, such as colonies before independence, Puerto Rico, or Greenland, are not added to any state. Smaller border changes within a state (for example Goa or Sabah and Sarawak) follow WPP’s current borders.

NMC’s documented -9 missing-data sentinel is recoded to NA in nmc_tpop and nmc_upop.

Fariss, Anders, Markowitz, and Barnum’s replication files contain one row per country-year for each underlying source indicator (e.g. Bairoch, Penn World Table, World Bank) plus one "latent_*" row holding the model’s combined estimate. load_gdp_data(dataset = "fariss") and load_population_data(dataset = "fariss") keep only the "latent_gdp" / "latent_gdppc" / "latent_pop" rows. Their absolute units are not independently verified in this package; consult Fariss et al. (2022) before using fariss_gdp, fariss_gdppc, or fariss_pop outside of relative/comparative analysis.

The SIPRI workbook lists a small number of rows (e.g. “Africa”, “NATO”) that are regional or organizational aggregates rather than countries; these have no matching COW/Gleditsch-Ward code and are dropped.

Barnum, Fariss, Markowitz, and Morales’s military expenditure replication file contains one row per country-year for each of 24 underlying source indicators, each in its own original currency/unit, with no single combined value on a real monetary scale (unlike the Fariss GDP/population files, the paper does not publish the shared latent trait directly because “the average by itself does not have a real or direct monetary unit”). Instead, load_military_expenditure_data(dataset = "barnum") reports the model’s posterior estimate of two specific indicators: barnum_sipri ("milex_con_2022_sipri") and barnum_nmc ("milex_con_2017_nmc"), which extend each one’s coverage back to 1816 using information from all 24 sources. Both are in constant (inflation-adjusted) dollars, so barnum_nmc is not directly comparable to nmc_milex from dataset = "nmc", which NMC documents in current-year dollars; their ratio varies smoothly over time (around 2.4 for the United States in 1990, falling toward 1 by the mid-2010s) rather than reflecting disagreement between the sources. barnum_milburden (milexgdp) is a unit-free ratio of spending to GDP and so is published directly.

Licensing

The package’s MIT license applies to the software, not to third-party data. Gapminder and UCDP identify their bundled data as CC BY 4.0; NAVCO 2.1, NAVCO 3.0, MEC, and ARC 2.0 are CC0; UN WPP is CC BY 3.0 IGO; OMG is released under the Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-BY). Other source files, including NMC, SIPRI, and the Fariss et al. and Barnum et al. estimates, retain their creators’ terms — SIPRI in particular is free to use with attribution but requires separately negotiating a royalty for commercial use. See inst/COPYRIGHTS and verify the applicable terms before redistributing a package build containing those files.
